topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cellular transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and classifications of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the definitions of cancer gene mutations and illustrate how alterations in tumor suppressors and oncogenes disrupt cellular regulatory pathways.

topics.label: Forms and molecular mechanisms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failures in specific DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer syndromes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer develops through the sequential acquisition of genetic alterations and how germline mutations accelerate this progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture, offers to answer questions, and recommends supplementary reading material.
